excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
You can look here: https://leanvm.org/

But TLDR, we are currently looking at:

- 8 threads reserved
- 5 GB RAM reserved
- AVX2 needed, AVX512 preferred
- conforms to 7870 CPU strength

Proofs will be around 300KB, proof times around 1.5 seconds.

This can/will be improved in the future, but I would say this is a baseline

an option I _tend to_ like is a system that has built-in elasticity to degrade gracefully .. it's easy to build a system that works well under optimal conditions but then goes into a death spiral under stress - this is something we often see in testnets for example, due to various reasons (mostly because we rarely test the "stressed" case and therefore don't spend as much time on ironing out bugs) ..

so for crypto, I would consider it a key feature that work is done incrementally and that "partial progress" still can be used, albeit with degraded rewards for example - degraded is better than nothing in stress scenarios because it can better get the system as a whole out of it .. 

in bls for example, we can play with latency vs cpu by batch-validating more signatures - on a weak cpu, we can do larger batches and still participate meaningfully

excerpts.content:
Bandwidth results from earlier this year are here. Not as bad as I feared.
<https://ethstaker.org/staking-landscape-analysis-2026/#bandwidth-advertised-max-available-up-amp-down>

Advertised upload bandwidth <100 Mbps for 23% of respondents to that survey

We didn't survey CPU or RAM. I'll work on a fresh survey.

For this to be useful, how long do you want the survey to run? A week? Two? As in, by when do you want to have an idea, vs. giving people time to become aware?

Tbh there is a long tail of people filling it out, but the bulk will likely be in 1-2 weeks

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
2-3 weeks would be good to get a representative set!

Perhaps we can keep it open since PQ EL(mempool propagation and aggregation) would also benefit from these numbers too
